title: fuel-efficient driving
objectives: Explain fuel-efficient driving techniques that let you drive smart and save money
Identify vehicle maintenance practices that help conserve fuel
List commercial vehicle components and features that help make a vehicle more fuel efficient
State how driving habits, idling and trip planning affect fuel consumption

sections.title: Why fuel efficiency matters and making smart choices
points: Fuel-efficient driving controls fuel costs and reduces greenhouse gas emissions.
Nearly 30 per cent of all greenhouse gas emissions in Canada are produced by vehicles.
Fuel-efficient driving techniques can improve fuel economy by up to 30 per cent.
Fuel-efficient driving is also safe driving: look ahead, keep space margins, anticipate hazards.
Smart practices include trip planning, maintenance and inspections, proper starting, proper driving, and reducing idle time.
mustKnow: Nearly 30 per cent of all greenhouse gas emissions in Canada are produced by vehicles.
Fuel-efficient driving techniques can improve fuel economy by up to 30 per cent.

check.q: Approximately how much can fuel-efficient driving techniques improve fuel economy?
check.explanation: The manual states fuel-efficient driving techniques can improve fuel economy by up to 30 per cent.

check.q: About what share of greenhouse gas emissions in Canada is produced by vehicles?
check.explanation: Nearly 30 per cent of all greenhouse gas emissions in Canada come from vehicles.

sections.title: Preparation, planning and starting the engine
points: Use the correct fuel for the season; summer fuel can improve economy but causes cold-weather engine problems.
Consider biodiesel: similar power, less carbon dioxide and sulfur, low particulate emissions.
Plan routes to avoid heavy commuter traffic, busy city driving and hills; flat highway routes are most efficient.
Snow-covered roads can increase fuel consumption by 15 to 20 per cent; adjust speed and following distance.
Start with zero throttle and never pump the throttle; it wastes fuel.
Warm up three to five minutes only, or seven to 10 minutes below 0 degrees C.
Check oil and air pressure rise to normal ranges; use ether sparingly and only if permitted.
mustKnow: Summer fuel can improve fuel economy by as much as three per cent.
Driving on snow-covered roads can increase fuel consumption by 15 to 20 per cent.
Warm up the engine three to five minutes only, or seven to 10 minutes if below 0 degrees C.
A flat multi-lane highway improves fuel efficiency four to 11 per cent over a flat two-lane, up to 18 per cent over mountainous, and 25 to 35 per cent over suburban roads.

check.q: How long should you let a heavy-duty diesel engine warm up when the temperature is below 0 degrees C?
check.explanation: Warm up three to five minutes normally, but seven to 10 minutes when the temperature is below 0 degrees C.

check.q: By how much can driving on snow-covered roads increase fuel consumption?
check.explanation: The manual states snow-covered roads can increase fuel consumption by 15 to 20 per cent.

sections.title: Smart driving techniques and reducing idling
points: Accelerate slowly after warm-up, keeping engine rpm down for several kilometres.
Practise progressive shifting, run in the highest gear range, and always use the clutch.
Back off the throttle over hill crests, use cruise control where appropriate, and reduce average speed.
Use see-think-do to anticipate hazards and keep a constant speed; power not used is fuel not burned.
Keep at least five seconds behind the vehicle ahead at highway speeds.
Anticipate stops and traffic lights; easing off the throttle beats braking at the last minute.
Turn the engine off when stopped for any length of time; idling wastes fuel and money.
mustKnow: Shifting gears properly can improve operating costs by 30 per cent.
Driving 105 km/h instead of 90 km/h is 15 per cent faster but consumes about 20 per cent more fuel.
Large heavy vehicles should never be less than five seconds behind the vehicle ahead at highway speeds.
Idling can burn up to four litres of fuel per hour; cutting one hour a day saves over 1,000 litres and over $1,500 per year at $1.50 per litre.

check.q: How much fuel can idling burn per hour?
check.explanation: Idling can burn up to four litres of fuel per hour.

check.q: Driving at 105 km/h instead of 90 km/h consumes about how much more fuel?
check.explanation: You travel 15 per cent faster but consume about 20 per cent more fuel.

sections.title: Maintenance and choosing a fuel-efficient vehicle
points: Regular maintenance keeps fuel efficiency up; fix small problems before they become big.
Inflate tires to manufacturer's recommendations and check fluid levels; do pre-trip, enroute and post-trip inspections.
Conduct enroute inspections, including tires and cargo, at least every three hours.
Choose the right truck for the job; a lighter truck carrying the same payload saves fuel.
Aerodynamic features like sloped hoods, roof fairings, trailer side skirts and gap reducers cut fuel use.
Rib tread tires beat lug tread on drive and steering axles; super-singles lower rolling resistance and weight.
Keep flatbed loads low and tarped; accessories like block heaters and on-board computers help efficiency.
mustKnow: For every 10 p.s.i. (69 kPa) a tire is underinflated, one per cent of fuel is wasted.
Conduct enroute inspections, including tires and cargo, at least every three hours.
Low-viscosity lubricants such as synthetic motor oil can improve fuel economy by up to four per cent.
At 90 to 100 km/h, about 50 per cent of fuel consumed is used to overcome air resistance.
Aerodynamic features can improve fuel economy by 15 to 20 per cent.

check.q: How much fuel is wasted for every 10 p.s.i. (69 kPa) that a tire is underinflated?
check.explanation: For every 10 p.s.i. (69 kPa) of underinflation, one per cent of fuel is wasted.

check.q: At speeds between 90 and 100 km/h, about how much of the fuel consumed is used to overcome air resistance?
check.explanation: About 50 per cent of fuel consumed at 90 to 100 km/h goes to overcoming air resistance.

summary: Fuel-efficient driving can improve fuel economy by up to 30 per cent and is also safe driving.
Plan routes, use seasonal fuel, and warm up three to five minutes (seven to 10 below 0 degrees C).
Drive smoothly: progressive shifting, steady speeds, five-second following distance, and anticipate stops.
Turn the engine off when stopped; idling burns up to four litres of fuel per hour.
Maintain tires, fluids and filters, and choose aerodynamic, properly specified vehicles to save fuel.
